ops.rationale: Names the compared representations by one term without 'pipeline', calls ARI near zero 'chance level', defines patient-grouped and the silhouette at their first use, splits the 46-word sentence and cuts the editorialising line on naive pipelines.
ops.new_text:
\begin{abstract}
Unsupervised analysis of the electrocardiogram (ECG) promises label-free
discovery of cardiac structure, yet whether clustering succeeds depends less on
the algorithm than on how the signal is represented. We benchmark four
representation families for unsupervised separation of sinus rhythm (SR) from
atrial fibrillation (AF) on PTB-XL: \rev{whole-record} raw flattening, a convolutional
\rev{autoencoder (conv-AE)}, compact hand-crafted rhythm and morphology features,
and two frozen foundation-model embeddings (HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder).
\rev{Evaluation is chance-corrected (adjusted Rand index, ARI) and patient-grouped, so that
no patient appears in more than one fold. It is repeated over ten seeds for the
clusterers that depend on one and bounded by a supervised ceiling, the accuracy a
supervised probe reaches on the same features.} ECGFounder clusters
best (ARI up to 0.885), but 16 interpretable hand-crafted features are competitive
(0.711) and far ahead of \rev{raw flattening and the conv-AE, which cluster at chance level
(ARI $\approx 0$). The conv-AE does so despite a supervised ceiling of 0.678, and raw
flattening has a ceiling of 0.519 against a majority-class baseline of 0.504.}
The same ordering holds on a MIT-BIH beat-morphology task. Two cautions emerge\rev{. The
silhouette score, a label-free index of cluster compactness, rewards the degenerate
one-cluster solution (silhouette 0.81 at ARI 0.000) and cannot validate ECG clustering
alone. Feature scaling, the per-feature transformation applied before clustering, moves
the mean ARI of the hand-crafted features from 0.229 to 0.629 across four scalers.
Under heavy class imbalance, at a 9:1 SR:AF ratio, the hand-crafted features have the
highest ARI, ahead of ECGFounder (0.265 against 0.063).
Under federation across ten sites that differ in class prevalence they retain the largest
share of their centralized ARI, 0.92 against 0.69 for ECGFounder, at about one fifteenth
of its inference time per record.}
\end{abstract}

ops.rationale: Opens the Introduction with the unsupervised clinical questions, splits the account of the master's project into its own paragraph, and gives the authors' work and decisions to 'we'.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Some clinical questions about the electrocardiogram (ECG) are unsupervised: which
patients group together, what subtypes exist, and whether structure can be found without
labels that are expensive or unavailable. On the two arrhythmia tasks we evaluate, whether
clustering of the ECG recovers a clinical label depends on the representation fed to the
clustering algorithm and on how the result is evaluated. A natural first attempt is to
cluster the records directly.}

\rev{We began this study as a re-examination of an unpublished master's project that did so.
That project flattened each 12-lead record into a long vector, compressed it with a dense
autoencoder, and clustered the code.
It reported high cluster purity, the share of the majority class inside each cluster, and
a silhouette score near 0.89, the silhouette being a label-free index of cluster
compactness.
Neither number measured agreement with the classes: the purity equalled the
majority-class proportion in every setting, and the silhouette was measured on a
degenerate solution in which almost all records fell into a single cluster.
The project's conclusion, that the difficulty lies in processing the raw signal rather
than in the clustering step, is correct, and we make it precise here.}

ops.rationale: Defines linear-evaluation accuracy and ARI where they first appear, names the MIT-BIH data source by its proper name, replaces 'arm' with 'representation' and gives the contribution to 'we'.
ops.new_text:
A representation can carry information about a label and still fail to cluster by it.
Linear separability and clusterability are distinct properties: a representation may
place the discriminative direction far from its dominant axes of variation, so that a
supervised probe recovers the label while an unsupervised partition does not.
\rev{Representations with nearly the same linear-evaluation accuracy, the accuracy of a
linear classifier trained on the frozen representation, can differ in how well they
cluster, as reported for self-supervised image encoders \cite{sslclustering2025}.
We treat the distinction as background.} What
has not been measured, for ECG, is how the common representation families compare on
this axis under proper chance-corrected metrics.
\rev{The most directly related work compares four ECG foundation models with one another
and with no hand-crafted baseline \cite{lookingbeyond2026}. It includes a
cluster-separability analysis (adjusted Rand index, ARI) of embeddings drawn from four
12-lead datasets, PTB-XL among them. Those datasets do not include the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia
Database.}
\rev{We add both: a hand-crafted representation built from RR-interval and beat-morphology
features \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}, and a beat-morphology task on the MIT-BIH
Arrhythmia Database \cite{mitbih2001}.}

ops.rationale: Replaces the punchy contribution lines with a plain statement, gives the authors' expectation and credit to 'we', names the raw representation and the original project consistently, defines Yeo-Johnson power scaling and non-IID at first use, uses 'class prevalence', and gives the scaling effect as the measured range.
ops.new_text:
We therefore benchmark four representation families for unsupervised SR-versus-AF
separation \rev{(sinus rhythm versus atrial fibrillation)}, with the controls the original
\rev{project} lacked. \rev{Because SR and AF differ by definition in the regularity of the
rhythm, we expected compact hand-crafted features and a large foundation model both to
recover the split. We therefore do not count the ordering of the representations among
the contributions.} Our contributions are modest and empirical\rev{, and they concern what
the controls show and how the representations behave under deployment stress:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] A chance-corrected, patient-grouped and significance-tested clustering
benchmark of raw flattening, a convolutional autoencoder (conv-AE), hand-crafted features
and two frozen foundation-model embeddings. Patient-grouped means that no patient appears
in more than one fold. Each representation is bounded by a supervised ceiling, the
accuracy a supervised probe reaches on the same features, and we show that the comparison
is stable across the assumed number of clusters.
\item[(ii)] Two reproducible methodological cautions that explain the original project's
misleading numbers. Internal validity indices such as the silhouette, which are computed
without labels, reward the degenerate collapse. Feature scaling, the per-feature
transformation applied to a representation before clustering, moves the mean ARI of the
hand-crafted features from 0.229 to 0.629 across four scalers. The four are Yeo-Johnson
power scaling, a per-feature power transformation fitted towards a Gaussian shape, and
standard, quantile and robust scaling.
\item[(iii)] The behaviour of the representations under two independent deployment
stressors: heavy class imbalance, and federation across sites that differ in class
prevalence (not independent and identically distributed, non-IID). The 16 hand-crafted
features have the highest ARI at a 9:1 SR:AF ratio and retain the largest share of their
centralized ARI under non-IID federation.
\item[(iv)] A generalization check on a MIT-BIH beat-morphology task, the data\-set the
closest prior benchmark omits.
\end{enumerate}
\end{revblock}
We do not propose a new method. \rev{The statements about foundation models concern
HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder, the two evaluated here, and we credit the
separability-versus-clusterability phenomenon to prior work.}

ops.rationale: Replaces 'underpin decades of automatic analysis' and 'general representations from millions of recordings' with what the cited sources show, and moves the study's scope, the second idea of the paragraph, to the opening of Section 3.2 (OP008).
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Unsupervised ECG and representations.} Hand-crafted features built from
RR-interval irregularity and beat morphology encode the defining signatures of common
arrhythmias\rev{. The standards of heart rate variability measurement define the
RR-interval statistics \cite{hrvstandards1996}, and RR-interval and morphology features
together served automatic heartbeat classification \cite{dechazal2004}.}
Tensor and wavelet decompositions have been combined with spectral clustering for
unsupervised 12-lead classification \cite{wavelettensorecg2018}. \rev{A reconstruction
autoencoder is trained to reproduce its input and receives no class information, so
nothing in its objective arranges its code by class.} \rev{Contrastive self-supervised
methods built on physiologically motivated augmentations and patient- or lead-level
invariances, including CLOCS \cite{clocs2021}, 3KG \cite{threekg2021} and contrastive
predictive coding for 12-lead ECG \cite{mehari2022ssl}, learn ECG representations without
labels.} Self-supervised and foundation models for
ECG, such as HuBERT-ECG \cite{hubertecg2024}\rev{, pretrained by self-supervision on
12-lead records,} and ECGFounder \cite{ecgfounder2024}\rev{, pretrained on more than ten
million recordings, are now evaluated as frozen feature extractors.} The wavelet-tensor and spectral-clustering pipeline of
\cite{wavelettensorecg2018} addresses a related unsupervised goal with a different
(tensor) representation.

ops.rationale: Names which models the closest benchmark found aligned with the labels and which with the dataset, in the wording the source supports, and gives the supervised ceiling to 'we'.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Closest benchmark.} \rev{The ECG foundation-model benchmark of
\cite{lookingbeyond2026} reported cluster-separability (ARI) of foundation-model
embeddings pooled over four 12-lead datasets, PTB-XL among them. In that analysis the
HuBERT-ECG and ECG-JEPA embeddings preserved structure tied to the dataset of origin and
separated the clinical labels less well, whereas the ECGFounder and ECG-FM embeddings
aligned more closely with the labels. The benchmark compared
foundation models to one another and stated that prior work omits a representation-wise
evaluation. It did not add a hand-crafted baseline, and it did not include MIT-BIH. Beyond
these two additions, we add a supervised ceiling so that a low clustering score
can be attributed to geometry rather than to missing information.}

ops.rationale: Calls PTB-XL a dataset, describes the input signals without software wording, and gives the per-representation choice of leads and preprocessing to 'we'.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{PTB-XL.} \rev{We used PTB-XL \cite{ptbxl2020}, a public dataset of 10\,s
12-lead records, in its version 1.0.3 release, which holds 21\,799 records from 18\,869
patients. Rhythm labels were taken
from the SCP-ECG (Standard Communications Protocol for Computer-Assisted
Electrocardiography) statements. The SR-versus-AF cohort used as positives all records
carrying an AF statement, atrial fibrillation (AFIB) or atrial flutter (AFLT), so that both
count as AF, and as controls the sinus-rhythm records without any AF statement.}
PTB-XL encodes rhythm statements at a likelihood of zero meaning ``present'' \rev{\cite{ptbxl2020}},
\rev{so a presence-based rule was required, since a confidence threshold would have
discarded every SR record. We drew} a balanced, patient-disjoint cohort of 2\,542 records
(1\,282 SR, 1\,260 AF), so the majority-class baseline is 0.504. \rev{Records were read
from the WFDB-format files of the \mbox{100\,Hz} release of the dataset, each as 1000
samples by 12 leads. No filtering, resampling or rescaling was applied before each
representation's own preprocessing, so every representation started from the same
signals. We chose the lead set and any further preprocessing per representation rather
than once for the whole study, and state them with each representation below.} All evaluation \rev{was} patient-grouped: no
patient appears in more than one fold or in both classes.

ops.rationale: Opens 3.2 in the past tense with the scope moved from Related work in the authors' voice, names raw flattening and the original project by one term each and ties the table label raw-flatten to it, replaces the unsupported 'properly specified' claim with the conv-AE's training facts, drops software wording, marks the missing source for lead II, and states in Methods that ECGFounder received upsampled 100 Hz data.
ops.new_text:
\rev{We compared four families on PTB-XL (Table~\ref{tab:main}). They range from
representations shaped only by signal energy, raw flattening and the conv-AE, to features
built from the defining signatures of the classes, and they include two frozen foundation
embeddings. We did not include a tensor representation \cite{wavelettensorecg2018} and
leave it to future work. The four families were built as follows:}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Raw flattening} \rev{(raw-flatten in the tables and figures)} reproduces
the \rev{input of the original project}: each lead \rev{was}
mov\-ing-average downsampled and all leads \rev{were} concatenated into one vector
($\sim$2000 dimensions). It carries amplitude and energy but no \rev{cross-record}
temporal alignment. \rev{Input: all twelve leads, 1000 samples by 12 leads. A
non-overlapping six-sample mean per lead left 166 samples per lead and a
1992-dimensional vector. This representation treats the sample amplitudes as the features
and imposes no clinical model on the signal. All twelve leads entered because raw
flattening reproduces the original project, which concatenated every lead.}
\item \textbf{Convolutional autoencoder} (conv-AE): a 1-D convolutional autoencoder
with a 32-unit bottleneck, trained \rev{with early stopping on a validation split, with
the settings given below. It replaces the dense autoencoder of the original project with
a convolutional one.} \rev{Input: all twelve leads, resampled to 12 by 2500 and z-scored per lead.
A reconstruction objective compresses whatever carries signal energy, which need not be
what separates the classes.}
\item \textbf{Hand-crafted} (16 features): RR-interval statistics and irregularity
\rev{(the standard deviation of the RR intervals (SDNN), the root mean square of successive
RR differences (RMSSD), the proportion of successive RR differences above \mbox{50\,ms}
(pNN50), the coefficient of variation, RR entropy and mean heart rate)}, P-wave
presence and amplitude, QRS width and amplitude, and beat-template consistency\rev{,
[GAP: one-clause definition of beat-template consistency, from the study's feature
extraction]} \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}, extracted with NeuroKit2
\cite{neurokit2021}. \rev{Input: lead II alone, 1000 samples, reduced to 16 features per
record. R-peak detection and wave delineation were performed on that one lead. Lead II is
the standard rhythm lead, on which RR regularity and P-wave presence are read [GAP: a
source for lead II as the standard rhythm lead]. Automated AF detection from a single short lead has been
benchmarked in a dedicated classification challenge \cite{clifford2017af}. A single-lead
definition also lets the feature logic, RR timing and beat morphology, be carried to the
two-lead MIT-BIH beats as the 21-dimensional beat-morphology set, where a twelve-lead
definition would not apply. The representation measures the AF signature directly, RR
irregularity together with P-wave absence.}
\item \textbf{Foundation embeddings} (frozen): mean-pooled hidden states of HuBERT-ECG
(768-d) \cite{hubertecg2024} and the 1024-d pooled features of ECGFounder
\cite{ecgfounder2024}, both used as fixed feature extractors with no fine-tuning.
\rev{Input: all twelve leads. HuBERT-ECG received the first \mbox{5\,s} at
\mbox{100\,Hz}, flattened lead-major into a 6000-sample vector. ECGFounder received the
full \mbox{10\,s} record of the \mbox{100\,Hz} release, upsampled to 12 by 5000 for its
\mbox{500\,Hz} input and z-scored once over all leads and samples together. Its input was
therefore upsampled \mbox{100\,Hz} data in place of the native \mbox{500\,Hz} data the
model expects, and Section~\ref{sec:limitations} compares the two on a 300-record subset.
Both lead sets are fixed by the published models,
which are defined on the complete twelve-lead record. The pretrained models supply a
fixed ECG feature space, and the question is whether that space places the rhythm
classes in separate regions.}
\end{itemize}

ops.rationale: Reports the lead choices in the past tense with 'representation' in place of 'arm', moves the interpretation of the raw result to the Results (OP023), and brings the conv-AE training and foundation-model inference paragraph from 3.3 into 3.2 (deleted there by OP011).
ops.new_text:
\rev{The representations used different lead sets, and each choice answered a different
constraint. The hand-crafted features used lead II alone, for the reasons given above.
Raw flattening used all twelve leads because the original project did, and it therefore
received more input than the hand-crafted features. Its twelve-lead input also made its
vector 1992-dimensional. On MIT-BIH the PTB-XL rhythm features do not carry over to single
beats, so the comparison there was between a raw beat window, a 21-dimensional
beat-morphology and RR-context feature set, and the conv-AE. The two foundation models
were not applied to the 2-lead beats, because both are tied to the 12-lead input format.}

\rev{The conv-AE was trained with Adam at a learning rate of \mbox{$10^{-3}$}, batch size
64, for at most 50 epochs on a 90/10 train/validation split. Training stopped when the
validation reconstruction error had not improved for eight epochs, and the
best-validation weights were restored. The two foundation models were applied with their
published weights frozen. HuBERT-ECG was mean-pooled over time from its last hidden layer
at batch size 64, and ECGFounder returned its globally average-pooled 1024-dimensional
feature layer at batch size 32.}

ops.rationale: Joins the 25-word paragraph on library defaults and deterministic clusterers to the clusterer paragraph it belongs to, expanding HDBSCAN at its new first use, and marks the missing neighbour count of the spectral affinity graph.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Each representation was clustered with five algorithms as implemented in scikit-learn
\cite{sklearn2011}, with the number of clusters set to the number of classes. Tolerances
and iteration caps were the library defaults, and no early stopping was imposed on the
clusterers. Ward agglomerative clustering and hierarchical density-based spatial
clustering of applications with noise (HDBSCAN) are deterministic given the input matrix,
so each was fitted once rather than once per seed. The five algorithms were:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{itemize}
\item $k$-means, with ten restarts per seed.
\item Ward agglomerative clustering, with Ward linkage on Euclidean distance.
\item Spectral clustering, with a nearest-neighbour affinity [GAP: number of neighbours of
the affinity graph] and $k$-means label assignment.
\item A Gaussian mixture model (GMM) with diagonal covariance and a covariance floor of
\mbox{$10^{-4}$}, since a full covariance is singular for the high-dimensional
representations.
\item HDBSCAN \cite{hdbscan2013}, with a minimum cluster size of $n/50$ rounded down and
floored at 10, with $n$ the number of records. On the PTB-XL cohort this is 50 records.
\end{itemize}
\end{revblock}

ops.rationale: Removes the conv-AE training and foundation-model inference paragraph from 3.3; OP009 places the same text in 3.2 Representations.
Deletes the paragraph on physical units, which restates the Range and Reading columns of the metrics table; the metric paragraph and the notation list stay unchanged.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The headline metrics were the chance-corrected adjusted Rand index (ARI)
\cite{hubertarabie1985} and adjusted mutual information (AMI) \cite{vinh2010}.
Normalized mutual information (NMI), V-measure, Fowlkes-Mallows, purity, silhouette
\cite{rousseeuw1987}, and the largest-cluster fraction were reported alongside. Every
metric was computed against a majority and a random baseline. Table~\ref{tab:metrics}
gives each reported metric with its definition, its range, and how a value on it is read,
in this notation:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{itemize}
\item $U$ is the partition by true class and $V$ the partition by cluster.
\item $n$ is the number of records and $n_{ij}$ the number of records in class $i$ and
cluster $j$.
\item RI is the fraction of record pairs on which $U$ and $V$ agree.
\item $I$ and $H$ are mutual information and entropy, with $\bar{H}$ the arithmetic mean
of $H(U)$ and $H(V)$.
\item $E[\cdot]$ is the expectation under the permutation model that holds both sets of
group sizes fixed.
\item $a_k$ and $b_k$ are the mean distance from record $k$ to the rest of its own
cluster and to the nearest other cluster.
\end{itemize}
\end{revblock}

ops.rationale: Turns the five controls run as prose into a list introduced with a colon, defines Yeo-Johnson power scaling and the other three scalers in the Methods, and marks the missing random-forest settings and the missing size and drawing of the 9:1 subsample.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Each result was read against four controls on the representation and on the clustering
set-up, and under one deployment stressor, class imbalance:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Supervised ceiling.} The supervised ceiling is the accuracy a probe reaches
on the same features under the same patient-grouped five-fold protocol. We report both a
linear probe (balanced logistic regression) and a non-linear probe (random forest, [GAP:
number of trees and the other settings of the random forest]), so that a high ceiling with
a low ARI identifies a geometric rather than an informational failure.
\item \textbf{Seeds.} Each configuration was repeated over ten seeds, and the headline
contrasts were tested with a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test across seeds.
\item \textbf{Feature scaling.} Because heavy-tailed features can dominate Euclidean
distance, we swept four scalers:
\begin{itemize}
\item Yeo-Johnson power scaling, a per-feature power transformation fitted towards a
Gaussian shape
\item standard scaling, to zero mean and unit variance per feature
\item quantile scaling, which maps each feature through its quantiles onto a fixed
reference distribution
\item robust scaling, which centres each feature on its median and divides it by its
interquartile range
\end{itemize}
We report power scaling as the default unless stated otherwise. Each scaler was fitted on
the full representation matrix, and any hand-crafted feature a record left undefined was
filled with that feature's cohort median before scaling.
\item \textbf{Number of clusters.} To check that fixing the cluster count to the number of
classes does not flatter the comparison, we also report adjusted mutual information, which
is comparable across cluster counts, for $K$ from 2 to 8.
\item \textbf{Class imbalance.} Because the natural SR-to-AF prevalence is imbalanced, we
additionally evaluated on a 9:1 SR:AF subsample [GAP: size of the subsample and how its
records were drawn].
\end{itemize}
\end{revblock}

ops.rationale: Removes the result sentence with the colloquial 'sat at the bottom' from the Methods; OP017 reports the same HDBSCAN result in 4.1 in formal wording.
ops.new_text:
\rev{HDBSCAN labels records it does not assign to any dense region as noise, and the
metrics treated that label in two ways. ARI, AMI, NMI, V-measure and Fowlkes-Mallows
received the prediction unchanged, so the noise records formed one further group of their
own and were charged against the agreement with the true partition. Purity and the
silhouette were computed on the assigned records only, because neither is defined for a
set that is not a cluster, and the purity denominator stayed the full cohort. Noise
records were never dropped from the evaluation and never reassigned to a nearest cluster.}

ops.rationale: Replaces the colloquial 'pinned at its floor' and the term 'arm' for a representation.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Each paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test was reported with two effect sizes. With ten
paired seeds the two-sided p-value falls to its floor of 0.002 as soon as every seed
moves the same way, so it separates none of the contrasts and cannot express a magnitude.
Cliff's delta gives the dominance of one representation over the other across all
cross-seed pairs, on a scale from $-1$ to $1$, and the matched-pairs rank-biserial
correlation rescales the signed-rank statistic itself onto the same scale. Each headline
contrast additionally carried the paired difference in ARI with its own patient-grouped
bootstrap interval.}

ops.rationale: Uses 'class prevalence' for how the classes are distributed across sites, defines Lloyd iterations, and splits the 49-word sentence on the federated rounds.
ops.new_text:
\rev{To probe deployment under data siloing we used federated $k$-means, with the centroids
aggregated in the manner of federated averaging (FedAvg) \cite{fedavg2017}. The 2\,542 records were partitioned,
patient-grouped, across ten simulated sites, either independently and identically
distributed (IID) or with each class's records spread over the sites in proportions drawn
from a Dirichlet distribution, so that the sites differ in class prevalence (non-IID). The
Dirichlet concentration was 0.3, applied per class over the ten sites, and any site left
holding fewer records than clusters was dropped. Feature scaling was fitted once on the
full representation matrix before partitioning, so the federation concerns the clustering
step alone. Each federated clustering consisted of fifteen aggregation rounds. In each
round every site performed three local Lloyd iterations, the assignment and
centroid-update steps of $k$-means. The server then replaced each centroid by the mean of
the site centroids, weighted by the number of records each site assigned to it. The
centroids were initialised globally from two randomly drawn records. Both settings were
repeated over ten seeds, with the site partition and the centroid initialisation redrawn
at each seed.} We report the
global ARI relative to centralized clustering of the same representation.

ops.rationale: Calls ARI near zero 'chance level' and names raw flattening without 'pipeline'; adds as a paragraph of its own the HDBSCAN and spectral results moved from the two-idea paragraph B0046 (deleted by OP021), with the clusterers named in place of 'Both', the 39-word sentence split, and the HDBSCAN result moved from the Methods (OP014).
ops.new_text:
\rev{On PTB-XL the choice of representation moved the best ARI from 0.008 for the conv-AE
to 0.885 for ECGFounder (Table~\ref{tab:main} and Fig.~\ref{fig:heatmap}). Within each of
the two representations that clustered well, the four clusterers other than HDBSCAN moved
it far less, from 0.709 to 0.885 for ECGFounder and from 0.544 to 0.711 for the
hand-crafted features. ECGFounder clustered best (ARI up to 0.885 with $k$-means) and the
hand-crafted features were competitive (0.711 with agglomerative clustering). HuBERT-ECG
was weak (0.195), and raw flattening and the conv-AE clustered at chance level
(ARI $\approx 0$).}

\rev{HDBSCAN and spectral clustering were applied with the settings of
Section~\ref{sec:clustering}, without further tuning. HDBSCAN had the lowest ARI on every
representation, shared on raw flattening, with 0.137 on ECGFounder and 0.060 on the
hand-crafted features. At its minimum cluster size it assigned only a minority of the
cohort on these two representations. On raw flattening, the conv-AE and HuBERT-ECG it
labelled the entire cohort as noise, which left one group and an ARI of exactly zero.
Spectral clustering reached an ARI of 0.016 on HuBERT-ECG, against 0.174 with $k$-means on
the same matrix, and 0.001 and 0.000 on the conv-AE and raw flattening
(Table~\ref{tab:main}).}

ops.new_text:
\rev{Each adjacent contrast between representations under $k$-means favoured the
representation higher in the ordering in every seed, and its paired bootstrap interval
excluded zero. A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the $k$-means seeds confirmed every
adjacent contrast, ECGFounder over hand-crafted ($\Delta = 0.242$, paired bootstrap
interval [0.202, 0.280]), hand-crafted over HuBERT-ECG ($\Delta = 0.470$, [0.424,
0.515]), and HuBERT-ECG over raw flattening ($\Delta = 0.174$, [0.146, 0.203]), at $p = 0.002$. That
value is the floor for ten paired seeds described in Section~\ref{sec:clustering}, so each
contrast also carries two effect sizes. Cliff's delta and the matched-pairs rank-biserial
correlation were both 1.00 on all three: every cross-seed pair and every signed rank
favoured the representation higher in the ordering. The magnitudes are therefore read from
the paired differences and their intervals. Moving only the seed left the $k$-means
partitions almost unchanged. The spread reported with the results is therefore the
patient-grouped bootstrap given in the caption of Table~\ref{tab:main}. Its intervals
separate every pair of representations except raw flattening and the conv-AE.}

ops.rationale: Cuts the closing sentence that repeats the values and the opening point, and replaces 'the raw pipeline' with 'raw flattening'.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The ordering does not depend on fixing the cluster count to the number of classes.
With adjusted mutual information for $K$ from 2 to 8, ECGFounder led at every $K$, from
0.825 at $K=2$ to a minimum of 0.441 at $K=7$ and 0.450 at $K=8$. The hand-crafted
features fell monotonically from 0.557 to 0.329, HuBERT-ECG stayed at or below 0.132, and
raw flattening never exceeded 0.005.}

ops.rationale: Splits the two-idea paragraph by relocation: the clusterer results go to 4.1 (OP017) and the contrast of the two foundation models, with the source's specific finding, to the ceiling paragraph (OP022).

Hedges the inference about ECGFounder's axes of variation and drops its ', so' shape, carries the figure reference of the deleted 4.2 paragraph, and closes on the two foundation models with the specific finding of the closest benchmark.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Each representation's position follows from two things: how much of the label its
space holds, which the supervised ceiling in the last column of Table~\ref{tab:main} and
Fig.~\ref{fig:sep} measures, and where in the space that label lies. The hand-crafted
representation is 16-dimensional and each coordinate is a quantity by which the classes
are defined, RR irregularity and P-wave presence. Its ceiling was 0.942 and an
unsupervised partition recovered 0.711. ECGFounder had the highest ceiling, 0.983,
recovered the most, 0.885, and led at every $K$ from 2 to 8. This suggests that the
rhythm split is one of the larger sources of variation in its 1024 dimensions. HuBERT-ECG
had almost the same ceiling as the hand-crafted features, 0.899, and recovered 0.195. The
two foundation models therefore did not behave as one category. This matches the report
of \cite{lookingbeyond2026} that HuBERT-ECG embeddings preserve structure tied to the
dataset of origin, while ECGFounder embeddings align with the clinical labels.}

ops.rationale: Hedges the conv-AE interpretation, gives the raw-flattening explanation a hedge and the discriminant-test result as its support without the repeated 'A likely reason' opener, drops the ', so' shapes, the colloquial 'sat at' and the closing one-liner, uses 'chance level', and takes in the input-size reading moved from the Methods.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The conv-AE and raw flattening showed two different ways for a representation to fail.
The conv-AE reached a supervised ceiling of 0.678 and an ARI of 0.008. A bottleneck
trained to reconstruct the signal may retain this much of a class it was not trained on
without arranging it into clusters. A linear probe on raw flattening reached 0.519 against
a majority-class baseline of 0.504 and found little label information in the
1992-dimensional vector. Its coordinates are amplitudes at fixed sample offsets, and a
fixed offset need not fall on the same part of the cardiac cycle in two records. This
misalignment may explain the low linear ceiling. The out-of-fold discriminant test below
agrees with that reading: no single direction fitted on other patients raised the
held-out ARI of raw flattening. Missing input does not explain the result, since raw
flattening received all twelve leads and the hand-crafted features one, although its 1992
dimensions may themselves weaken Euclidean clustering. Both representations were at chance
level under all five clusterers, raw flattening for want of linearly accessible label
information and the conv-AE because its code holds more without arranging it into
clusters.}

ops.rationale: Deletes the 4.2 paragraph whose values 4.1 already gives and whose citation stands in the Introduction; its unsupported 'properly trained' claim, unhedged off-axis claim, 'raw pipeline' and 'at chance' go with it, and its figure reference moves to OP022.
Names the gap in the opening sentence, now the first of 4.2, rewrites the three ', so' interpretations in other shapes, replaces 'sat below' and names raw flattening by one term.
ops.new_text:
\rev{A non-linear probe showed that the gap between the supervised ceiling and the ARI is
not an artefact of a linear probe. On raw flattening the random forest reached 0.714
against a linear ceiling of 0.519 and a clustering ARI of 0.000: a non-linear decoder
recovered a label that clustering did not. The same probe gave 0.951 on the hand-crafted
features, 0.983 on ECGFounder and 0.825 on HuBERT-ECG. On the two representations that
clustered well it added little over the linear ceiling, 0.951 against 0.942 for the
hand-crafted features and 0.9835 against 0.9831 for ECGFounder. Their label information
was therefore already linearly accessible. Probe linearity does not explain HuBERT-ECG's
gap either, since there the random forest lay below the linear ceiling of 0.899.}

ops.rationale: Rewrites the opening ', so' interpretation, replaces 'comparison arm', and follows the 0.013 difference with what it means for the comparison.
ops.new_text:
\rev{A single discriminant direction estimated from other patients more than tripled
HuBERT-ECG's held-out ARI. This indicates that its class information is present and lies
off its dominant axes of variation. In this out-of-fold test, a linear discriminant was
fitted on the training patients of a patient-grouped stratified five-fold split, the
held-out patients were projected onto that single axis, and the projection was clustered
with $k$-means without labels. The baseline of the test was $k$-means on the same
held-out records in their native representation. Fitting the discriminant on every label
and then clustering the projection would recover the labels by construction, which is why
the projected patients were held out. Over five folds and ten seeds, on 508 or 509
held-out records per fold, the mean ARI rose from 0.160 to 0.549 for HuBERT-ECG, from 0.003
to 0.121 for the conv-AE, from 0.646 to 0.758 for the hand-crafted features and from 0.893
to 0.923 for ECGFounder, and did not move for raw flattening, 0.000 to 0.001. These are
held-out values, so the native column does not equal the full-cohort $k$-means ARIs of
Table~\ref{tab:main}. The largest difference is 0.013, on HuBERT-ECG. The held-out native
values keep the order of the full-cohort values, which makes the gains from the
projection comparable with Table~\ref{tab:main}.}

ops.rationale: Reports the paragraph in the past tense, replaces 'arms' and the colloquial 'rose off chance', and gives the conv-AE reading as a hedged interpretation in place of the ', so' shape.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The native and projected values separated furthest for HuBERT-ECG, and its gain
showed that its class information transfers across patients. HuBERT-ECG also received only
the first \mbox{5\,s} of each \mbox{10\,s} record, about half the RR intervals the other
representations received, which may contribute to its low native ARI alongside this
off-axis reading. ECGFounder gained almost nothing, because its dominant axes already
carried the split. The ARI of the conv-AE rose above chance level but stopped far short of
its ceiling of 0.678, which suggests class structure that is both off-axis and diffuse.
Raw flattening did not move at all, which separates its failure from HuBERT-ECG's: no
single direction estimated from other patients separated the classes in it, and whatever
the non-linear probe recovered from it was not of that form.}

ops.rationale: Supports the robust-scaling explanation with the definition of the scaler in place of the repeated 'A likely reason' opener, keeps one hedge, and gives the reporting choice to 'we'.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Feature scaling changed the outcome by a wide margin. For the hand-crafted features
the mean ARI over clusterers was 0.629 under standard scaling and 0.606 under power
scaling, but fell to 0.360 under robust scaling and 0.229 under quantile scaling. The
effect was not confined to the hand-crafted features: ECGFounder's mean ARI dropped from
0.866 (standard) to 0.093 under robust scaling. Robust scaling divides each feature by its
interquartile range, which the records in a heavy tail do not affect, and those records
therefore keep large values after scaling. A few of them may then dominate Euclidean
distance, which would explain the fall under robust scaling. A clustering result on these
representations needs its scaler stated, and we report power scaling unless stated
otherwise.}

ops.rationale: Calls PTB-XL and MIT-BIH datasets, the one term for a data source.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The ordering replicated on a different dataset and a different task type
(Table~\ref{tab:mitbih}). On the N-vs-V beat-morphology task the 21-dimensional
beat-morphology features clustered well (ARI 0.783), whereas the raw beat window did not
(ARI 0.018 with $k$-means and 0.049 with agglomerative clustering) despite the beats being
R-peak aligned. The raw beat window still reached a supervised ceiling of 0.741, so it
held label information that clustering did not recover. The conv-AE was again the clean
separability-versus-clusterability case, with a supervised ceiling of 0.927 but a best ARI
of only 0.127, from the Gaussian mixture. That the same pattern appeared for rhythm on
PTB-XL and for morphology on MIT-BIH, on two datasets with different lead sets and class
definitions, supports the representation-level reading.}

ops.rationale: Opens the class-imbalance paragraph with its own point, leaving the federation result to the next paragraph, uses 'chance level', and adds the alternative reading that a two-cluster clusterer on a 9:1 cohort accounts for part of the drop and of the reversal.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Class imbalance moved the hand-crafted features ahead of ECGFounder. At the
natural-like 9:1 SR:AF ratio (majority 0.90), every representation's ARI fell. These
results used power scaling and [GAP: the clusterer of the 9:1 results, which the
manuscript does not name], over the ten seeds. The hand-crafted features retained the most
structure (ARI 0.265 [0.250, 0.280], AMI 0.245 [0.233, 0.257]) and \emph{overtook}
ECGFounder (ARI 0.063 [0.061, 0.065], AMI 0.148 [0.143, 0.152]), with no overlap between
the two ARI intervals. HuBERT-ECG reached the same ARI as ECGFounder (0.061 [0.053, 0.069])
at a lower AMI (0.044 [0.037, 0.050]). At this ratio its partition therefore agreed with
the classes on record pairs as often as ECGFounder's but shared less information with
them. Raw flattening and the conv-AE stayed at chance level (0.000 and 0.004). A clusterer
fixed to two clusters on a cohort with a 9:1 class ratio may divide the majority class
instead of separating the minority, so part of the fall may come from the clustering
set-up rather than from the representations. The reversal may likewise reflect how each
representation interacts with that set-up as well as the structure it holds, and it holds
for this ratio, scaler and clusterer, the only imbalanced setting evaluated.}

ops.rationale: Uses 'site partition' for a redrawn partition of the cohort into sites and 'chance level' for ARI near zero, and states the worst-partition criterion in those terms.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Under non-IID federation the three representations that cluster above chance level lost
unequal shares of their centralized ARI (Table~\ref{tab:fed} and Fig.~\ref{fig:fed}).
ECGFounder fell from 0.885 to 0.612, the hand-crafted features from 0.644 to 0.591 and
HuBERT-ECG from 0.174 to 0.106, while raw flattening stayed at 0.000 in every setting.
Under IID federation across ten sites every representation retained essentially its
centralized ARI, which validates the federated procedure. The hand-crafted features
retained 92\% of their centralized ARI, the largest share. ECGFounder's lead over them
narrowed accordingly, from 0.885 against 0.644 centralized to 0.612 against 0.591 under
non-IID federation. The two means were close, and they did not carry the same risk. Across
the ten redrawn site partitions the hand-crafted bootstrap interval was [0.546, 0.631] and
the worst single partition still reached 0.455, whereas ECGFounder's interval was
[0.382, 0.796] and three of its ten partitions fell to 0.132 or below, one of them to
chance level. We judge a deployment by the worst site partition as well as by the average
one, because a real federation has one partition of its records into sites, which may be
an unfavourable one. On that criterion the 16 hand-crafted features were the more
predictable of the two under site heterogeneity.}

ops.rationale: Uses 'site partitions' in the caption of the federation figure.

Opens with the paragraph's point, replaces the claim that cost and quality were ordered against each other with what Tables cost and main show, splits the 49-word sentence, and names the hand-crafted features in place of 'the hand-crafted path'.
ops.new_text:
\rev{ECGFounder, which clustered best, was the most expensive representation per record,
at about fifteen times the inference time of the hand-crafted features
(Table~\ref{tab:cost}). Cost and clustering quality were not ordered alike across the
other representations: HuBERT-ECG cost more per record than the hand-crafted features,
37.530 against \mbox{28.296\,ms}, and reached a best ARI of 0.195 against 0.711. Both
foundation models needed a gigabyte or more of resident memory, against \mbox{364\,MB}
for the hand-crafted features, which carry no learned parameters. Clustering itself was
negligible, under \mbox{0.3\,s} for the whole cohort at any of the five dimensionalities.
The cost of a representation was therefore the cost of extracting it.}

ops.rationale: Removes the one-line summary 'The lead constraint is concrete.' and joins its content to the sentence that gives the evidence.
ops.new_text:
\rev{For the PTB-XL rhythm task and the MIT-BIH morphology task, the results support a
decision rule.} If a strong public foundation model can be run on balanced data in the
target 12-lead format, ECGFounder gives the best unsupervised separation here. If the data
are imbalanced or siloed across sites, if interpretability or low dimensionality matters,
or if the leads on hand are not the standard twelve, the 16 hand-crafted features are the
better choice\rev{. On the PTB-XL cohort they were within reach of ECGFounder on balanced
data (0.711 against 0.885). They led it at the 9:1 ratio (0.265 against 0.063), the one
imbalanced setting evaluated. Under non-IID federation their retention was 0.92 against
0.69 for ECGFounder (Table~\ref{tab:fed}). The cost comparison of Table~\ref{tab:cost}
points the same way: the representation that held up better under both stressors is also
the lower-cost one to compute. The lead condition rests on the MIT-BIH task: the two
foundation models we tested could not be applied to its 2-lead beats, whereas the
hand-crafted feature logic carried to them as the 21-dimensional beat-morphology set.}

ops.rationale: Names the representations without 'pipelines', uses 'chance level', and places the decision-rule sentence directly after the result it follows from.
ops.new_text:
\rev{On PTB-XL raw flattening and the conv-AE clustered at chance level under all five
clusterers. On MIT-BIH, evaluated with three clusterers, the conv-AE reached at most 0.127
and the raw beat window at most 0.049, against 0.783 for the beat-morphology features. On
both tasks the raw input and the conv-AE recovered far less of the class structure than
the hand-crafted features on PTB-XL and the beat-morphology features on MIT-BIH. The
decision rule above therefore chooses only between ECGFounder and the hand-crafted
features. Raw flattening reproduces the input of the original project, and its PTB-XL
result gives that project's conclusion, that the difficulty lies in processing the raw
signal, in chance-corrected terms.}

ops.rationale: Replaces the second list of the Introduction's contributions with a Discussion paragraph that relates the results to the closest benchmark, which removes the closing editorial line and the term 'database'.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The closest ECG foundation-model clustering benchmark \cite{lookingbeyond2026}
compared foundation models with one another, and its reading of HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder
agrees with the ordering found here. The comparison with hand-crafted features changes
what that ordering means for a user: the foundation model that led on balanced data did
not lead at the 9:1 ratio, and its lead narrowed under non-IID federation. The supervised
ceilings qualify a low score: HuBERT-ECG held the label (ceiling 0.899) without
clustering by it (ARI 0.195), so a low ARI alone does not show that an embedding lacks
the clinical information. The MIT-BIH task, on a dataset that benchmark does not include,
showed the same advantage of features built from the class definitions over raw input and
the conv-AE for beat morphology.}

ops.rationale: Splits the 48-word and the closing long sentence, replaces 'axis' and 'arm' for the foundation-model family, and pairs each best ARI with its model.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The foundation-model family is bounded to two models by selection rather than by
survey. HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder both publish weights that load into a frozen feature
extractor without fine-tuning, which is what a benchmark of frozen embeddings requires.
They also differ in pretraining objective and architecture: HuBERT-ECG is a
self-supervised transformer \cite{hubertecg2024}, and ECGFounder a convolutional model
pretrained on more than ten million recordings \cite{ecgfounder2024}. Their best ARIs
here, 0.195 for HuBERT-ECG and 0.885 for ECGFounder, show that the two do not form a
single point. The bound scopes the conclusions: every statement here about a foundation
model is a statement about one of these two, the deployment comparison is between the
hand-crafted features and ECGFounder specifically, and none of it extends to ECG
foundation models as a class. A further model that clusters as well as ECGFounder on
balanced data would leave the results reported here unchanged. It would have to be
measured again under imbalance and under federation before the deployment reading could
be extended to it.}

ops.rationale: States the measured 0.013 difference without a hedge, replaces 'arm', and adds the limitation that the conv-AE conclusions rest on one architecture with one 32-unit bottleneck.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The learned representations are limited in the models they hold, and ECGFounder also
in its input rate. ECGFounder expects 500\,Hz input, and because the 500\,Hz release could
not be obtained in full for this study, the main benchmark embeds the 100\,Hz cohort
upsampled to the expected length. A comparison on a 300-record subset gave ECGFounder an
ARI of 0.909 with the upsampled 100\,Hz input and 0.896 with the native 500\,Hz input. On
that subset the upsampled input therefore gave ECGFounder an ARI 0.013 higher, which is
small against its $k$-means lead of 0.242 over the hand-crafted features. We evaluate two
foundation models. Other foundation models, including ECG-FM, which the closest benchmark
reports to separate by clinical label \cite{lookingbeyond2026}, are not included, and
Section~\ref{sec:discussion} sets out how this bounds the conclusions. The MIT-BIH
evaluation has no foundation-model row, for the lead reason given in
Section~\ref{sec:representations}. The conv-AE is likewise one architecture with one
32-unit bottleneck, and its results describe that configuration rather than reconstruction
autoencoders in general.}

ops.rationale: Gives the scope decision to 'we' in place of the passive 'is evaluated'.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Both evaluated tasks are binary by design, one rhythm contrast and one morphology
contrast, each chosen so that the class definition is unambiguous and a clustering failure
can be charged to the representation rather than to label noise. We evaluated no
multi-class arrhythmia cohort, and no result here is a statement about multi-class
arrhythmia structure, where several rhythms share an irregularity signature and the
largest class outnumbers every minority. A multi-class PTB-XL rhythm cohort over the same
embeddings is the least costly way to test whether the ordering survives that setting. The
AF class also includes atrial flutter, which can conduct with a regular ventricular
rhythm, so the flutter records among the AF positives may not fit the reading that SR and
AF differ in rhythm regularity.}

ops.rationale: Splits the 44-word sentence, uses 'chance level', and replaces 'by a wide margin' with the measured range.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The federated study simulates ten sites within one dataset. Its only control on
heterogeneity is the Dirichlet concentration, which moves class prevalence across sites
and nothing else. The spread that this alone produces is already wide: over the ten
redrawn non-IID partitions ECGFounder ranges from chance level to 0.881, while the
hand-crafted features stay between 0.455 and 0.643. Feature scaling in the simulation is
fitted on statistics pooled over all sites, which a real federation would not have, and
Section~\ref{sec:scaling} shows that the choice of scaler moved the mean ARI of the
hand-crafted features from 0.229 to 0.629.
Device vendor, lead placement, population case mix and local labelling practice also differ
between hospitals and are absent from the simulation. Settling their effect needs ECG
records held at several institutions, clustered under a federated protocol with the site
of origin retained as a variable, which was not available for this study.}

ops.rationale: Splits the 45-word sentence, uses 'site partitions' and 'chance level' without 'pipelines' or 'sit', and restricts the reporting recommendation to what the PTB-XL results show.
ops.new_text:
\rev{For unsupervised arrhythmia structure in the ECG, the spread of ARI across
representations exceeded the spread across clustering algorithms with\-in each
representation that clustered well, and chance-corrected external evaluation was required
to see it. This held on the two tasks evaluated here: SR-versus-AF rhythm separation in
PTB-XL and N-vs-V beat morphology in MIT-BIH. On balanced PTB-XL data ECGFounder,
pretrained on more than ten million recordings \cite{ecgfounder2024}, leads. At a 9:1
SR:AF ratio, 16 interpretable hand-crafted features overtake it. Under simulated
federation across ten heterogeneous sites they are the more predictable of the two,
retaining 0.92 of their centralized ARI against 0.69 and never falling below 0.455 over the
ten site partitions. On PTB-XL raw flattening and the conv-AE cluster at chance level under
all five clusterers. The silhouette rewards a degenerate solution there, and the choice of
scaler moves the mean ARI of the hand-crafted features from 0.229 to 0.629. On these
representations and this cohort a clustering result therefore needs its scaler stated and
its internal indices read against a chance-corrected index.
Whether these results hold for multi-class arrhythmia cohorts, for other foundation models
and for a real multi-institution federation is open.}

ops.rationale: Uses 'datasets', the one term for a data source, in the ethics statement.
